intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Most tours include snorkeling and swimming stops along the way.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and tiropita. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions dating back centuries.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner with Fresh Seafood in Mykonos
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in Little Venice, Mykonos, enjoying freshly grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes paired with Assyrtiko white wine. Watch the iconic windmills glow in the golden sunset light while savoring some of the freshest seafood in the Aegean.

experiences.name: Red Beach and Perissa Black Beach Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a day exploring Santorini's unique volcanic beaches. Start at the dramatic Red Beach with its striking red and black volcanic cliffs, then head to the long stretch of Perissa Black Sand Beach for swimming and relaxing at a beach bar. The contrasting colors and crystal-clear waters make this a truly unique Greek beach experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class at a local family farm in Crete, the birthplace of the Mediterranean diet. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The class includes a farm tour, olive oil tasting, and a full sit-down meal with local wine.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, take the X96 express bus or metro Line 3 to the city/transfer point toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and unwind after your flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick gyro wrap or spanakopita from a 24-hour kiosk near the airport or en route to the hotel (approx. €3–5).

day_by_day.notes: Keep travel light on Day 1. Pre-book your airport transfer or research the cheapest public transport route in advance. The X96 bus is one of the most budget-friendly options from Athens airport.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the beachfront outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm June morning sun, dip your toes in the sea, and get oriented with the local area. Explore the nearest village or harbor on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach (likely walking distance from the resort). Swim in the warm Aegean Sea, sunbathe, and relax. Rent a beach umbrella and sunbed if needed (approx. €5–8 for a pair) or bring your own towel and find a free spot.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade at sunset. Explore local tavernas and pick one for a sit-down dinner. Watch the sunset over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a simple breakfast at the resort or grab fresh koulouri (sesame bread rings) and a Greek coffee from a nearby bakery (approx. €2–3).
meals.lunch: Pick up a gyro pita or souvlaki from a local fast-food grill near the beach (approx. €3–4).
meals.dinner: Dine at a local taverna on the waterfront — order grilled octopus, Greek salad, and a carafe of house wine. Look for daily specials (approx. €12–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated — temperatures can reach 29°C. Buy a reusable water bottle and refill at local fountains or supermarkets to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the local open-air morning market (laiki agora) if one is held nearby. Browse fresh fruits, vegetables, olives, local cheeses, and honey. This is a great way to experience authentic Greek daily life and stock up on cheap, fresh snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby cove or lesser-known beach accessible by a short local bus ride or walk. These quieter spots are often free and less crowded than main tourist beaches. Swim and snorkel if you have gear.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely evening walk through the old part of the nearest town. Admire whitewashed buildings, bougainvillea-draped alleyways, and small chapels. Sit at a café for a frappe or freddo espresso.

meals.breakfast: Buy fresh fruit, local yogurt, and honey from the morning market (approx. €3–5 total).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from market finds — bread, olives, cheese, tomatoes — and enjoy it at the cove beach.
meals.dinner: Find a family-run taverna away from the main tourist strip for more authentic and cheaper food. Try moussaka or pastitsio with a local beer (approx. €10–13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ask locals or hotel staff for directions to the best hidden coves — they often know spots not listed online.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or cheap ferry to a nearby island or coastal town for a day trip. Explore the main harbor, browse local shops, and visit a hilltop viewpoint or old church for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming at one of the day-trip destination's best beaches. The water is warm and clear in June. Explore rock formations or sea caves if accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by early evening. Relax by the resort pool or take a sunset swim at the beach before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — Greek yogurt with honey or a cheese pie (tiropita) (approx. €3–4).
meals.lunch: Eat at a budget taverna at the day-trip destination — fresh fish of the day or a simple Greek salad with bread (approx. €10–14).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using market ingredients in a resort kitchenette (if available) or grab takeaway souvlaki near the hotel (approx. €5–7).

day_by_day.notes: Check local ferry or bus schedules the night before and buy tickets early to avoid queues. Day trips are often very affordable on local transport.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost guided walking tour of the nearest historic town or archaeological site. Many areas in Greece have ancient ruins, Byzantine churches, or Venetian fortresses within easy reach. Wear sunscreen and a hat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach club or popular sandy beach for the afternoon. Swim, people-watch, and enjoy the vibrant beach atmosphere. Try paddleboarding or kayak rental if budget allows (approx. €10–15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor cultural event, live music performance, or local festival if one is happening (June is peak season for local events). Otherwise, enjoy a quiet dinner at a harbor-side restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and Greek coffee from a local bakery (approx. €3).
meals.lunch: Eat at a beach snack bar — a simple toasted sandwich, tzatziki, and a cold drink (approx. €6–8).
meals.dinner: Try a mezedes (small plates) dinner at a local ouzeri — order 3–4 small dishes to share like taramosalata, dolmades, fried zucchini, and grilled sardines (approx. €12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Download the Google Translate app with Greek language for offline use — very helpful when reading menus or asking for directions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim before the beach gets crowded — the sea is calm and crystal clear in the mornings. Take a walk along the coastline and discover small fishing boats and local fishermen at work.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum or cultural site (entry fees are typically €3–8 for budget sites). Many Greek towns have small but fascinating archaeological or folk museums that give insight into the region's history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife scene on a budget — find a rooftop bar with a view and enjoy one drink at sunset, then move to a cheaper taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Prepare your own breakfast with supermarket finds — yogurt, fruit, bread, and local honey (approx. €2–3).
meals.lunch: Try a local psarotaverna (fish tavern) for affordable fresh catch — grilled fish with lemon, olive oil, and vegetables (approx. €12–15).
meals.dinner: Visit a neighborhood souvlaki shop for a filling and cheap meal — chicken or pork skewers with pita and tzatziki (approx. €5–8).

day_by_day.notes: Greece's first Sunday of each month offers free museum entry at state-run sites. Check if any free entry days fall during your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter for the day (approx. €10–20) and explore the surrounding countryside and coastline at your own pace. Discover olive groves, vineyards, and hidden chapels along rural roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded beach or lagoon spotted during your morning ride. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing in near-total solitude — a true Greek island experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes/scooters and head into town for the evening volta (evening stroll) — a beloved Greek tradition. Join locals walking the main street and end the night with a gelato or loukoumades (honey doughnuts).

meals.breakfast: Eat at a café near the bike rental — scrambled eggs, toast, and juice (approx. €5–7).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local mini-market — bread, olives, cheese, and fruit (approx. €4–6).
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional grill house (psistaria) — try lamb chops, village salad, and house wine (approx. €13–17 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Always wear a helmet when renting a scooter — it is legally required in Greece. Check that your travel insurance covers scooter rental.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip or water taxi to a nearby sea cave, blue lagoon, or uninhabited islet. Many local operators offer affordable group tours (approx. €15–25 per person). Snorkeling in the crystal-clear water is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the main beach for a relaxed afternoon. Read a book under an umbrella, swim, and recharge. Visit a beachside kiosk for cold drinks and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food tour if available locally (some budget options exist for approx. €20–30). Alternatively, visit a local winery or olive oil producer for a free or low-cost tasting.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with granola and fresh berries from a café (approx. €4–5).
meals.lunch: Eat on the boat trip if food is included, or grab a quick bite from a beach taverna upon return — a simple salad and grilled calamari (approx. €10–12).
meals.dinner: If you took a cooking class, enjoy what you made! Otherwise, try a local taverna specializing in Cretan or regional cuisine (approx. €12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book boat trips early in the morning for best prices — operators often discount unsold spots. Group tours are significantly cheaper than private charters.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or hilltop castle/fortress. Many of these are free or very low cost (€2–6) and offer stunning views of the sea and surrounding landscape. Go early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a popular sandy beach for the afternoon. Try beach volleyball if nets are available, or simply swim and snorkel. The sea temperature in June is perfect — around 24–25°C.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop restaurant or terrace taverna for dinner with a panoramic view. Share a bottle of local wine and enjoy the warm evening air.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and a freddo cappuccino from a local bakery (approx. €3–4).
meals.lunch: Eat near the archaeological site — pack sandwiches or find a small café serving simple Greek dishes (approx. €5–8).
meals.dinner: Order a traditional Greek feast — lamb kleftiko or slow-roasted pork with roasted potatoes, village bread, and local wine (approx. €14–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for archaeological sites — terrain can be uneven and rocky. Bring water and a portable fan or cooling spray for the midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a slow morning at the hotel beach — swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the peaceful early hours before tourists arrive. Practice some basic snorkeling if you have a mask and fins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus to a nearby town or village for afternoon shopping and exploration. Browse local craft shops for affordable souvenirs — olive wood items, ceramic plates, local spices, and honey make great gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a beach bar. Then head to a local taverna for your last few nights' worth of trying new dishes.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — eggs, olives, tomatoes, feta, and bread (approx. €6–8).
meals.lunch: Eat at a local village café — try gemista (stuffed tomatoes and peppers with rice) or fasolada (bean soup) (approx. €7–10).
meals.dinner: Visit a seafood restaurant and try grilled sea bream (tsipoura) or sea bass with lemon and olive oil (approx. €14–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is not typical in Greek shops, but asking for a small discount when buying multiple items is sometimes acceptable. Always check prices before ordering at restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise swim or early morning yoga session on the beach if the resort offers it. Enjoy the golden morning light reflecting off the Aegean Sea — a truly magical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local olive grove or traditional farm if accessible. Many farms in Greece welcome visitors for free or a small fee and offer tastings of olive oil, honey, and local products. Alternatively, visit a local monastery or Byzantine church.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate your penultimate full day in Greece. Choose a well-reviewed taverna and try dishes you haven't eaten yet during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, local honey, and a strong Greek coffee from a neighborhood bakery (approx. €3–4).
meals.lunch: Visit a traditional kafeneion (old-style Greek café) and order a simple mezedes spread with ouzo or tsipouro (approx. €8–10).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly upscale taverna meal — try lobster pasta (astakomakaronada) or a whole grilled fish shared between two people with local wine (approx. €18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Take time to reflect on your trip and jot down favorite memories and spots. This is also a good evening to pack non-essentials and begin organizing your luggage for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — take one last long swim in the warm Aegean, collect a small piece of sea glass or a smooth pebble as a free natural souvenir, and soak in the sun and scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping or revisit your favorite spots from the trip. Pick up local products like dried herbs (oregano, thyme), local wine, or small ceramic pieces to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite taverna from the trip. Order your favorite dishes, raise a glass of local wine, and toast to a wonderful Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — make it a proper sit-down meal to mark the last full day (approx. €6–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch — a fresh Greek salad with feta and a cold frappe at a beach café (approx. €7–9).
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite taverna from the trip for a memorable farewell meal. Order a dessert too — try galaktoboureko (custard pastry) or baklava with Greek coffee (approx. €15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure transport arrangements for the next day. Set an early alarm if your flight requires a long transfer. Pack your bags tonight to avoid morning stress.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early, take one final look at the Aegean Sea from your room or the beach, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Head to the airport or ferry port for your departure transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure day — travel to Athens International Airport or your departure point. Allow plenty of time for check-in, security, and any last-minute airport shopping for Greek products (olive oil, herbs, local sweets).
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight and reminisce about 13 incredible days in Greece — the beaches, the food, the warm sun, and the warm people.

meals.breakfast: Quick and easy breakfast before checkout — use up any remaining supermarket snacks or grab a pastry and coffee to go (approx. €3–4).
meals.lunch: Eat at the airport — try to find a Greek fast-food option like a gyro stand rather than expensive international chains (approx. €8–12).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snacks depending on your departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your receipts if you are eligible for VAT refunds on purchases over €50 from participating shops. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before an international flight. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration and collect baggage, then take a pre-arranged airport transfer or taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from a 24-hour hotel bar or room service upon arrival — keep it simple after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival, no sightseeing is planned. Confirm your transfer in advance and have the hotel's contact number saved. Drink water and rest well to prepare for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take your first walk along the beachfront to get your bearings — feel the warm Aegean sand and take in the stunning coastal scenery. Dip your toes in the sea for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's beach. The sea is warm and perfect for swimming. Rent a sun lounger, go for a long swim, or try snorkeling near the shoreline to explore the clear blue waters. Recharge and shake off any jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or waterfront promenade for your first proper Greek dinner. Explore the local tavernas and enjoy the relaxed Mediterranean atmosphere as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Greek yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Casual beachside snack at the resort's beach bar — try a Greek salad, club sandwich, or fresh fruit platter
meals.dinner: Local waterfront taverna — order grilled fresh fish, tzatziki, horiatiki (Greek salad), and warm pita bread. Budget around €20–30 per person with a glass of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — your body is still adjusting to the time zone. Apply sunscreen generously as the Greek sun at 29°C can be intense, especially mid-afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head out for a guided or self-guided walk through the local town or village near the resort. Visit the main square, browse small shops selling local products like olive oil, honey, and herbs. Pop into a local bakery for a mid-morning treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby beach that's slightly off the beaten path — ask hotel staff for a recommendation for a quieter cove or bay accessible by local bus or taxi. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the crystal-clear waters away from the main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and find a traditional ouzeri or mezedopoleio for dinner — a restaurant specializing in small shared plates (mezedhes) paired with ouzo or local wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — try spanakopita (spinach pie) or tiropita (cheese pie) if available alongside your usual spread
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local bakery or market — grab fresh bread, olives, local cheese (feta or graviera), and fruit. Enjoy it at the beach.
meals.dinner: Ouzeri dinner with mezedhes — order dolmades (stuffed vine leaves), grilled octopus, fava bean dip, and saganaki (fried cheese). Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Carry cash as smaller local eateries and bakeries may not accept cards. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning village exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip or water taxi to explore nearby sea caves, hidden coves, or a small uninhabited island if available in the area. Many coastal resorts in Greece offer half-day boat excursions departing around 9:00–9:30 AM. Book through the hotel concierge the day before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat trip and spend the mid-afternoon at leisure on the beach. Try paddleboarding or kayaking — rentals are typically available at the resort beach or nearby water sports centers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a clifftop or rooftop bar if one is nearby. Then head to dinner at a family-run taverna slightly inland for a more authentic and affordable experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the boat trip — fuel up with eggs, cheese, bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat if included, or grab souvlaki wraps from a local street food stall upon return — budget-friendly at €3–5 each
meals.dinner: Family taverna inland — try moussaka, pastitsio (baked pasta with meat), or lamb kleftiko. Budget €15–22 per person including a carafe of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat excursion at least one day in advance. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water for the boat trip. Sea conditions are generally calm in June.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local archaeological site, ancient ruins, or a hilltop castle within day-trip distance of the resort. Greece is rich with history even outside of Athens — ask the concierge about the closest ancient site. Explore with a self-guided audio tour or hire a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cultural morning, find a nearby beach or sheltered bay for a relaxing afternoon swim. The contrast of ancient history and modern beach bliss is quintessentially Greek.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the resort town's main harbor or marina area for the evening volta (the traditional Greek evening stroll). Browse waterfront restaurants and pick one that catches your eye for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Café or snack bar near the archaeological site — try a cheese or ham toastie, a Greek salad, or a cold frappé coffee
meals.dinner: Harbourside restaurant — enjoy fresh seafood such as grilled sea bream, calamari, or shrimp saganaki with a glass of crisp Assyrtiko white wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes for exploring ruins as ground can be uneven. Visit archaeological sites early in the morning before the heat peaks — aim to arrive by 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach morning — choose the best beach in the area (ask locals or hotel staff for their personal favourite). Arrive early to claim a good spot. Swim, read, and soak up the sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class or food tour in the afternoon if available locally — learn to make traditional Greek dishes like spanakopita, tzatziki, or loukoumades (honey doughnuts). Alternatively, visit a local olive oil producer or winery for a tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Light evening — pick up supplies from a local supermarket or deli (cheese, charcuterie, olives, local wine) and enjoy a private balcony or beach picnic dinner at the resort as the sun goes down.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Beach taverna or kiosk — try a grilled corn on the cob, fresh watermelon, or a simple toasted sandwich
meals.dinner: Self-curated balcony picnic — local feta, Kalamata olives, cured meats, crusty bread, cherry tomatoes, and a bottle of local wine. Budget €15–20 for two from a deli or supermarket.

day_by_day.notes: A cooking class is a wonderful mid-trip activity and a great way to connect with local food culture. Check with the hotel concierge for recommendations and bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or coastal town — take a ferry, catamaran, or organized excursion. Greece's coastline offers countless gems within a short boat ride. Explore the new destination's streets, beaches, and viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the day-trip destination — swim at a local beach, visit a monastery or chapel, and browse artisan shops for unique souvenirs like hand-painted ceramics, woven textiles, or local spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Have a quiet dinner close to the hotel — you'll likely be pleasantly tired from a full day of exploring.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna in the day-trip destination — try whatever the local specialty is. In many Greek islands this could be fresh lobster pasta, grilled sardines, or chickpea soup.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the resort — a simple gyros wrap or souvlaki plate from a local grill house. Budget €10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry or boat schedules in advance and book tickets the day before if possible. Bring a light layer for the boat ride back in the evening as sea breezes can be cool after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after yesterday's day trip. Enjoy a slow breakfast, then take a gentle morning swim at the resort beach. Read a book in the shade or take a short coastal walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local market if there is a weekly market day — Greek laiki (street markets) are wonderful for fresh produce, spices, honey, local cheeses, and handmade goods. Pick up some treats to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a rooftop restaurant or a restaurant with a panoramic sea view for a special dinner. This is a good evening to splurge slightly on a nicer meal.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort — try Greek honey cake or bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) if available
meals.lunch: Fresh produce from the market — assemble your own mezze spread with market finds. Eat al fresco at a park bench or beach area.
meals.dinner: Upscale taverna or view restaurant — try lamb chops, stuffed peppers, or a seafood platter. Budget €30–40 per person for a treat. Pair with local Agiorgitiko red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Market days vary by location — ask the hotel concierge which day the local market runs. Bring a reusable bag and small cash for market shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Water sports morning — try jet skiing, parasailing, or windsurfing at the resort's water sports centre or a nearby beach club. The warm calm June sea is ideal for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off with a visit to a shaded village café for a long Greek coffee break — order a freddo espresso or a traditional Greek coffee and people-watch. Browse a local bookshop or gift shop.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset cruise if one is available from a nearby marina — many Greek coastal areas offer 2–3 hour sunset boat tours with wine and light snacks included. A magical way to spend the evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Village café lunch — try a toasted sandwich, Greek salad, or a cold mezze plate. Enjoy the slow pace of Greek café culture.
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the sunset cruise — a souvlaki plate or mezze spread at a casual local spot. Budget €12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset cruise through the hotel concierge or at the marina. Prices typically range from €35–55 per person and often include wine, water, and light snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different beach today — hire a scooter, take a local bus, or join a taxi to reach a more remote or scenic beach in the region. Greece is full of hidden beaches accessible only by a short hike or boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a long, lazy afternoon at the secluded beach — swim, snorkel, and explore the coastline. Bring your own picnic supplies from the hotel or a nearby shop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the hotel restaurant — a good opportunity to try their house specialties and enjoy the beachfront setting at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before heading out
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at the secluded beach — olives, cheese, bread, fruit, and plenty of water. Pick up supplies from a local mini-market before departing.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — try their signature dish or the catch of the day. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If hiring a scooter, ensure you have an appropriate licence and always wear a helmet. Alternatively, ask the hotel to arrange a private taxi for the day — often cost-effective when split between two people.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural morning — visit a local Byzantine church, traditional monastery, or folk museum in the area. Greece's cultural heritage extends far beyond ancient ruins and includes medieval, Byzantine, and Ottoman-era history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a beach club or a more upscale beach bar for a change of pace — enjoy a sunbed, cocktails, and good music. Many Greek beach clubs offer reasonable day passes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different part of the local town for dinner — try a neighbourhood you haven't visited yet. Look for a psarotaverna (fish taverna) for a seafood-focused dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the beach club — fresh salad, a smoothie bowl, or grilled chicken wrap
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna dinner — order whole grilled fish by weight (sea bass or sea bream are excellent), grilled prawns, and a Greek salad. Budget €22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: When ordering whole fish at a psarotaverna, the fish is priced per kilogram — ask the waiter to show you the fish and confirm the price before ordering to avoid surprises on the bill.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favourite beach of the trip for one last long swim and sunbathing session. Reflect on the trip and enjoy the warm Aegean water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration of the local area. Pick up gifts — Greek olive oil, thyme honey, mountain tea, local wine, ceramic pieces, or evil eye (mati) charms. Visit any spots you may have missed during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — choose the best restaurant you've discovered during your stay or try somewhere new that's been recommended. Make it a memorable final evening in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — savour it as one of your last mornings
meals.lunch: Casual beach snack or light café lunch to leave room for the big farewell dinner
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favourite or most-recommended restaurant — order generously and celebrate the trip. Try a Greek dessert like galaktoboureko (custard pastry) or loukoumades with honey. Budget €30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check if any shops or markets have specific closing days so you can plan your souvenir shopping accordingly. Many Greek shops close for a long midday break (roughly 2–5 PM) and reopen in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy one last breakfast at the resort. Take a short final walk along the beach to say goodbye to the Aegean Sea. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and transfer to the airport. Allow plenty of time for the journey and airport procedures. If your flight is in the late afternoon or evening, you may have time to stop at a café near the airport for a final Greek coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a suitcase full of local goodies.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort — enjoy every last bite of Greek yogurt and honey
meals.lunch: Airport café or restaurant — many Greek airports have decent options including fresh salads and sandwiches
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time with the hotel and arrange your airport transfer the evening before. Keep some euros for airport coffee, last-minute shopping, or tipping your driver. Kalό taxídi — have a great journey!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Most tours include snorkeling and swimming stops along the way.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and tiropita. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions dating back centuries.

experiences.name: Red Beach and Perissa Black Beach Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a day exploring Santorini's unique volcanic beaches. Start at the dramatic Red Beach with its striking red and black volcanic cliffs, then head to the long stretch of Perissa Black Sand Beach for swimming and relaxing at a beach bar. The contrasting colors and crystal-clear waters make this a truly unique Greek beach experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink at the resort bar, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the Aegean Bliss Resort — request a curated mezze board and a glass of chilled Assyrtiko white wine to unwind after your journey

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — rest is the priority. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge upon check-in. Request a wake-up call for a leisurely start the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast on your private balcony overlooking the sea. Take a refreshing morning swim in the resort's infinity pool or the warm Aegean Sea. Spend time orienting yourself with the resort's amenities — spa, beach club, and concierge services.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local coastal village on foot or by resort-provided bicycle. Browse artisan boutiques, pick up premium local olive oil and honey, and soak in the authentic Greek seaside atmosphere. Return to the resort for a late afternoon session at the beach club with sun loungers and cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset aperitivo at the resort's clifftop bar. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a full introduction to Greek cuisine — expect dishes like grilled octopus with fava purée, fresh sea bream, and loukoumades for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Greek breakfast buffet at the Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh pastries, local cheeses, honey, yogurt, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort beach club — grilled calamari, Greek salad with Kalamata olives, and freshly squeezed citrus juice
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — multi-course Greek tasting menu paired with curated Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Keep the pace relaxed. Ask the concierge to arrange spa treatments for the following morning if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a private yoga session on the beach at sunrise, arranged through the resort. Follow with a pampering 90-minute treatment at the resort spa — choose from a traditional Greek herbal massage or a sea-salt scrub using local ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a private chartered speedboat for an exclusive afternoon coastal cruise along the shoreline. Discover hidden sea caves, secluded coves, and crystal-clear waters. Anchor at a pristine private beach for snorkeling and swimming in the warm Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and refresh. Head to a highly regarded local taverna in the nearby village for a traditional Greek dinner in an authentic setting — candlelit, family-run, and beloved by discerning locals.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service — Greek yogurt parfait with thyme honey and walnuts, smoked salmon, fresh-pressed orange juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by the resort chef and enjoyed aboard the private boat — artisan bread, local charcuterie, stuffed vine leaves, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Acclaimed local taverna — slow-roasted lamb kleftiko, village horiatiki salad, and house barrel wine; finish with homemade galaktoboureko

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up for the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a full-day trip to Athens. A private luxury vehicle will transfer you to the nearest ferry port or airport for a quick connection to Athens. Upon arrival, head straight to the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) for an immersive guided food tour — sample local cheeses, cured meats, fresh spices, olives, and street food with an expert local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, enjoy a leisurely lunch at a celebrated Athens restaurant in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood. In the afternoon, visit the Acropolis and the Parthenon with a private guide — beat the crowds with a timed entry ticket and gain deep historical insight into ancient Greek civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sun set over Athens from a rooftop bar in Monastiraki with Acropolis views and cocktails in hand. Dine at one of Athens' top fine-dining establishments before your private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Quick but quality breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh pastries, Greek coffee, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Premium Athens restaurant near Monastiraki — modern Greek cuisine featuring dishes like tuna tartare with tarama, lamb chops, and eggplant imam
meals.dinner: Top-tier Athens fine-dining restaurant — chef's tasting menu with Greek wine pairings; consider Varoulko Seaside or Spondi for a Michelin-starred experience

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day trip — wear comfortable walking shoes for the Acropolis. Book Acropolis timed-entry tickets well in advance. Confirm private round-trip transfers with the concierge the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge after the Athens day trip. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort — swim in the sea, read on the beach, and indulge in a late breakfast. Optionally, book a private cooking class at the resort where a local chef teaches you to prepare traditional Greek dishes using market-fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach — rent a paddleboard or kayak, enjoy the warm 29°C weather, and simply bask in the luxury of the beachfront setting. Order refreshing drinks and light snacks from the beach butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private sunset dinner on the beach arranged by the resort — a table set directly on the sand with torchlight, curated menu, and dedicated service. A truly romantic and memorable Greek evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — full à la carte menu; try the traditional Greek breakfast with dakos, feta, tomatoes, and herbs
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — fresh grilled fish of the day, tzatziki, warm pita, and a refreshing watermelon and feta salad
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course curated menu featuring the day's freshest catch, paired with premium Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private beach dinner experience at least 48 hours in advance — it is one of the resort's most popular offerings and requires advance arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or ferry to Santorini — one of Greece's most iconic islands. Check in to a luxury cave hotel or caldera-view suite (pre-booked as an extension of your trip). Take in the breathtaking views of the volcanic caldera and the whitewashed Cycladic architecture of Oia and Fira.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Red Beach and Perissa Black Beach for an extraordinary volcanic beach experience. Start at the dramatic Red Beach near Akrotiri — the rust-red volcanic cliffs plunge directly into the vivid blue sea. Swim and snorkel in the clear waters before moving to the expansive Perissa Black Beach, where dark volcanic sand meets a lively beach club atmosphere with sunbeds and cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia village for the world-famous Santorini sunset — find a prime spot along the castle walls or enjoy the view from a private terrace. Dine at a premium caldera-view restaurant in Oia for an unforgettable evening.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast at your Santorini hotel — fresh fruit, Greek pastries, local honey, and strong Greek coffee with caldera views
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna at Perissa Black Beach — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and Greek salad with a cold Mythos beer or local white wine
meals.dinner: Upscale caldera-view restaurant in Oia — dishes like lobster pasta, grilled sea bass with lemon and capers, and Santorinian tomato fritters; paired with Assyrtiko wine

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is extremely popular in June — book all restaurant reservations well in advance, especially sunset-view spots in Oia. Wear sturdy sandals for the rocky path to Red Beach.

day_by_day.morning: Join a private guided tour of the ancient ruins of Akrotiri — Santorini's remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' A knowledgeable private guide brings the 3,600-year-old city to life. Follow with a visit to a premium Santorinian winery for a guided tasting of indigenous Assyrtiko wines grown in volcanic soil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a luxury beach club on Kamari Beach — enjoy premium sunbeds, cooling dips in the sea, and attentive service. Alternatively, book a private catamaran cruise around the caldera, stopping at the volcanic hot springs and the islet of Nea Kameni.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point — for panoramic island views at dusk. Dine at a celebrated restaurant in Fira or Imerovigli with sweeping caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with caldera views — Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh-squeezed juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Winery lunch at a Santorini estate — wine-paired mezze spread featuring local cheeses, cherry tomatoes, capers, and fava dip
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant in Imerovigli — modern Greek tasting menu with volcanic island ingredients; try the Santorini fava with truffle oil and the slow-cooked lamb with local herbs

day_by_day.notes: The Akrotiri archaeological site is covered and air-conditioned — a welcome relief on hot days. Pre-book the private catamaran cruise through your hotel concierge for best availability.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry or short flight to Zakynthos (Zante) — home to some of Greece's most spectacular beaches. Check in to a luxury beachfront villa or boutique hotel. Freshen up and head to the beach for a morning swim in the famously turquoise Ionian Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the highlight experience of Zakynthos — a private boat tour to Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach). Accessible only by sea, this iconic cove features a rusted shipwreck on a pristine white pebble beach enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs. Swim in the electric-blue waters, explore the wreck, and take in one of Greece's most photographed landscapes in relative exclusivity on a private vessel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the main island and explore the charming Zakynthos Town waterfront. Enjoy an evening stroll along the esplanade before settling in for dinner at a highly regarded local restaurant specializing in Zakynthian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at a local café near the port before departure — fresh koulouri, local cheese pie, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic aboard the private boat at Navagio Beach — prepared by your villa or hotel; enjoy it on the beach with the shipwreck as your backdrop
meals.dinner: Acclaimed Zakynthos Town restaurant — Zakynthian specialties such as sofrito (veal in garlic-wine sauce), bianco fish stew, and mandolato nougat for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach can only be reached by boat — book your private boat tour in advance. Arrive early in the afternoon to avoid the peak tourist rush from larger group boats. The beach has no shade, so bring a hat and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise kayaking or paddleboarding excursion along the dramatic Zakynthos coastline — the light at this hour is extraordinary. Visit the famous Blue Caves on the northern tip of the island, where sunlight refracts through the sea to create an ethereal blue glow inside the sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gerakas Beach — one of Zakynthos' finest and a protected nesting site for Loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta). Swim in the calm, clear waters and keep an eye out for turtles. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine beach with premium sunbed service.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your villa for a private in-villa dining experience — arrange for a local private chef to prepare a traditional Zakynthian feast in the comfort of your accommodation, served under the stars.

meals.breakfast: In-villa or hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt with local honey, fresh fruit, and warm pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna near Gerakas — fresh grilled fish, village salad, and cold white wine
meals.dinner: Private chef in-villa dinner — a curated four-course Zakynthian menu featuring local seafood, seasonal vegetables, and premium Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has strict regulations to protect sea turtle nests — do not disturb marked nesting areas and avoid the beach after dark during nesting season. Book the private chef at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at your Zakynthos accommodation — swim, sunbathe, and recharge. Check out and take a ferry or flight back to the mainland or to your next island. Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort for your final nights of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle back into the Aegean Bliss Resort. Spend the afternoon at the resort's beach club — enjoy the warm sea, order refreshing cocktails, and reflect on the journey so far. Book a late afternoon massage at the resort spa to soothe any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely dinner at the resort's premier restaurant. Try dishes you haven't yet sampled from the menu — perhaps a whole roasted fish, fresh pasta with local seafood, or a chef's special inspired by the season.

meals.breakfast: Final Zakynthos breakfast at a local café — fresh-baked tiropita, local honey, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch upon return — mezze platter, hummus, warm pita, and a chilled glass of rosé
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort fine-dining restaurant — seasonal tasting menu; ask for the chef's recommendation and a Greek wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport from Zakynthos to the resort well in advance. Allow buffer time for ferry schedules, which can occasionally run late in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a deep-dive into local Greek food culture. Arrange a private market visit to the nearest village market with a local food expert — discover seasonal produce, artisan cheeses, fresh herbs, and regional specialties. Follow with a hands-on Greek cooking class led by a celebrated local chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: After cooking class, enjoy the meal you prepared for lunch. Spend the afternoon on a leisurely boat trip to a nearby secluded beach only accessible by sea — swim, snorkel, and enjoy the pristine waters in total tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sundowner at the bar. Dress for dinner and head to the most acclaimed restaurant in the region — make this a special celebratory evening with a premium tasting menu and exceptional Greek wine list.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with freshly baked bread, local jams, eggs to order, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your cooking class — a deeply personal and authentic Greek meal
meals.dinner: Region's top fine-dining restaurant — reserve the chef's table if available; expect elevated Greek cuisine with premium local ingredients and an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is best booked through the resort concierge who can connect you with top local chefs. This is a wonderful opportunity to take home recipes and culinary skills as a lasting souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full morning making the most of the Aegean Bliss Resort's luxury facilities — a long swim in the sea, a final spa treatment, or simply reading on your private balcony with a coffee in hand. Soak in the views and the warmth of the Greek sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic afternoon drive or guided tour to a nearby historic site, monastery, or hilltop village — discover the cultural and historical layers of the region beyond the beach. Return to the resort in time for a final golden-hour swim in the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Host your own private farewell dinner on your suite's terrace — arrange with the resort for a romantic in-room dining setup with your favorite dishes from the trip and a bottle of premium Greek wine. Reminisce about the highlights of 13 extraordinary days in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final resort breakfast — order everything you loved throughout the trip; savor every last bite
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional village taverna during your afternoon excursion — simple, honest Greek food at its best; grilled meats, village salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at your suite — curated by the resort chef; a personalized farewell menu with your favorite dishes from the trip and a premium Greek wine

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort to arrange a special farewell amenity — many luxury properties offer a complimentary dessert, wine, or keepsake for departing guests. Pack tonight to make tomorrow morning stress-free.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy one final Greek breakfast at the resort — take your time, breathe in the sea air, and cherish the last moments of your luxury Greek escape. Take a final walk along the beach or a last dip in the Aegean Sea before checking out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. A private luxury transfer will take you to the airport or port for your onward journey. Stop at a local shop en route to pick up premium Greek souvenirs — extra virgin olive oil, aged thyme honey, saffron from Kozani, or fine Greek wine to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you the flavors, memories, and warmth of 13 unforgettable days in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely resort breakfast — Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh pastries, and a proper Greek coffee to send you off in style
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a café near the port — pick up a fresh spanakopita or tyropita for the journey
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for check-out and transfer to avoid any last-minute rush. Confirm your departure transfer with the concierge the evening before. Keep a small bag accessible for any last-minute beach or café stops en route to the airport.
